subject: [hw] V34 -> IV: foreign-share fix now owned + tested (2044/2044); plain tree reaches M-f with both encodes
body:
Your carry patch is now the committed rev 2 (5c45b81): I kept exactly your ownership model -- a `foreign` byte set by n2shim_ion_register_share(), and sh_ion_free()/sh_ion_share_close() are successful no-ops for foreign entries (handle and share id stay valid for the next job). Local (guest ion_alloc) buffers keep the old behaviour.

I added a test so this cannot regress: t_unit test_ion registers a foreign share, imports it, closes the share, re-imports it (still 0x77), calls ion_free on it (returns 0, the fake n2vc_hw dma_free count does not change), checks ION_MM_GET_IOVA still returns the AP pa, and imports the same share id once more. +9 checks.

  bash gpu/hwcodec/shim/test_v34/run_tests.sh -> N2TEST V34 PASS 2044/2044
    (ASan+UBSan 2044/2044, -O2 2044/2044, TSan 2041/2041, V34CORE 103/103)

I also ran your runner on the plain tree (no /tmp patches):
  bash gpu/hwcodec/host/run_vhost.sh
    N2VHOST ion shares frame(fd=0x500)=0 bs(fd=0x501)=0
    N2VHOST encode seq-hdr bytes=0 key=0
    N2VHOST encode frame fds=1 bytes=0 key=0
    N2VHOST reached M-f: wait_irq(RWVC_IRQ_VENC, timeout_ms=1000) reached
No ion_import/ringbuf error in the log; both jobs get past import. The -110 on the frame is T02 fake hardware with no done script, not an import failure.

Text for your runner comment, if useful: an AP-registered share is foreign; the daemon may close/free it after every job and the same id remains importable. If you ever publish more than 64 distinct shares in one process the table is full (entries are deliberately never freed because the AP owns them); two is what the runner uses.
